title: Social Preferences and Cooperation: Beliefs, Robustness, and the Limits of Altruism
abstract: arXiv:2609.11374v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study a mechanism of cooperation in the Prisoner's Dilemma (PD). Incorporating social preferences as efficiency concerns into the PD game, we study how altruism translates into cooperation. Under complete information, cooperation requires the opponent's altruism to clear a threshold. We then introduce a subjective extension of Bayesian Nash equilibrium that relaxes the Common Prior Assumption, letting players hold heterogeneous, potentially misspecified beliefs about each other's altruistic type. Cooperation then depends on beliefs about altruism rather than altruism itself, and can be sustained even when opponents are, on average, only weakly altruistic. When fear of exploitation dominates the temptation to defect, beliefs about the opponent's cooperation become strategic complements, so a cooperative and an uncooperative equilibrium can coexist under identical payoffs and an identical, correctly specified prior. translated_title: 社会偏好与合作：信念、稳健性与利他主义的局限
translated_abstract: 我们研究囚徒困境（PD）中的合作机制。通过将社会偏好作为效率关注引入囚徒困境博弈，我们探讨利他主义如何转化为合作。在完全信息条件下，合作要求对手的利他程度超过某一阈值。随后，我们引入贝叶斯纳什均衡的一种主观扩展形式，放松了共同先验假设，允许参与者对彼此的利他类型持有异质的、可能存在偏差的信念。在这种情况下，合作取决于对利他主义的信念而非利他主义本身，即使对手平均而言仅具有微弱的利他主义，合作仍可维持。当对被剥削的恐惧压倒背叛的诱惑时，关于对手合作的信念成为策略互补品，因此合作均衡与不合作均衡可以在相同的收益和相同的、正确设定的先验信念下并存。利用乘数先验……（摘要截断）
tldr: 本文将社会偏好引入囚徒困境博弈，提出放松共同先验假设的主观贝叶斯纳什均衡，证明合作取决于对他人利他主义的信念而非利他主义本身，从而揭示了合作与不合作均衡在相同收益和先验下并存的机制。
en_tdlr: This paper incorporates social preferences into the Prisoner's Dilemma and introduces a subjective extension of Bayesian Nash equilibrium that relaxes the Common Prior Assumption, showing that cooperation depends on beliefs about altruism rather than altruism itself, thereby explaining how cooperative and uncooperative equilibria can coexist under identical payoffs and priors.
